html:
SMTO-SKL-0014 — SMTO needs you to sign in to Google Calendar again

GUID: 2fcbc463-7b2e-5a1d-8f33-caec44c2d769
Slug: google-calendar-reauthorization-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • Google no longer accepts SMTO's saved sign-in for this account. This can happen after a password change, removed access or an expired approval. Your calendar wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to reconnect your Google account for Calendar, and open the Google link it gives you. Google stops accepting a saved sign-in after a password change, removed access or an expired approval, and a fresh approval replaces it.
  2. On Google's page, check that the email address shown is the same account SMTO used before, then allow the Calendar access it lists. Approving a different account won't repair the sign-in for this one, and SMTO won't switch accounts for you.
  3. Ask SMTO to check the Google account's connection status, then ask for the calendar task again. Google refused the earlier request, so it's safe to ask again once the account shows as connected.

What success looks like

  • The connection status shows the account as connected with Calendar access, and the task completes.

If it still fails

  • Your Google administrator may have blocked SMTO's access. Select Copy error details and send them to that administrator or the person who manages SMTO. Don't sign in with a different account in place of this one.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google returned 401 for the Calendar request even after one forced token refresh, or the selected google_account's authorization_state is not available (for example disconnected or revoked).

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 401 or the selected account's authorization_state is not available. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 401 or the selected account's authorization_state is not available.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect saved authorization state and the recorded provider response.

How to fix it

  • Reconnect the same google_account with auth.google_connect or google_calendar.connect (same auth_app_ref and account_key), then confirm its granted Calendar features with google_calendar.connection_status before another operation. If 401 persists, check whether the grant was revoked in the Google account or by Workspace policy.
  • Reconnect the same shared Google account and verify its Calendar features before another operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reconnect the same shared Google account and verify its granted Calendar features before another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • Reconnecting the same intended account restores the required granted features.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
